I read the whole file (lines 1–130) and checked it only against the "repeated proof machinery" rubric. I did not open any other source files. The file has six proofs, and none repeats nontrivial reasoning that a shared lemma could replace.

- `IsSelfAdjoint.map_spectrum_real` is an Urysohn and functional-calculus argument. It is used once, by `map_quasispectrum_real` and `norm_map`. The quasispectrum version only reduces to the unitization and calls it, so it doesn't repeat the argument.
- `toOrderEmbedding` proves that an injective map reflects order, using the quasispectrum characterization of positivity. Its only repeated element is the short `sub_nonneg` rewrite, which is routine.
- `map_le_map_iff` and `map_lt_map_iff` are one-line wrappers around `toOrderEmbedding`. `nnnorm_map` and `isometry` are also one-line wrappers around `norm_map`. Those are thin wrappers over existing API, which the rubric excludes.
- `norm_map` has a single spectral-radius calculation, so nothing in it repeats.

I found no justified finding. The remaining uncertainty is that I didn't search the rest of Mathlib for similar arguments outside this file, but the rubric concerns repetition across proofs in this file.
